seoDescription: Step-by-step guide to install and serve language models locally with vLLM on Ubuntu using an NVIDIA GPU. Learn how to set up a Python virtual environment, install vLLM, PyTorch, and Hugging Face CLI, obtain a read token, download and serve models (example: Code Llama 2.5 coder), and call an OpenAI-compatible local endpoint. Covers VRAM considerations, throughput features like batching, flash attention, quantization options, and practical inference examples.

summary:
## Key Concepts

- **vLLM**: A high-throughput, production-ready engine for serving large language models locally or on a network via an OpenAI-compatible API.

- **Environment setup**:
  - Create a Python **virtual environment** to keep dependencies isolated.
  - Install **vllm**, **PyTorch**, and **huggingface-hub** (plus torchvision/torchaudio if needed).

- **Hugging Face integration**:
  - Download models from Hugging Face. Grab a **read token** from your profile when models require authentication.
  - Use the **Hugging Face CLI** to log in for gated models.

- **Serving and API**:
  - vLLM serves an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (e.g., localhost:8000/v1) so existing OpenAI clients work with minimal changes.
  - Instantiate an **OpenAI client** against the local endpoint and send prompts as usual.

- **Performance and optimizations**:
  - vLLM supports **continuous batching**, **flash attention**, and **flash inference** to maximize throughput.
  - You can run models in **full precision** or use **quantization** (GPTQ, AWQ, 4-bit, 8-bit, FP8) to reduce memory use and increase speed.
  - **Chunked prefill** and other memory strategies help fit large models in GPU memory.

- **Practical tips**:
  - Monitor **VRAM** consumption; multiple models or leftover processes can inflate usage.
  - Use simple curl or OpenAI client examples to validate the server is running and returning responses quickly.

> [!TIP] For initial experiments pick an un-gated model so you can download without authentication, then test gated models after configuring the Hugging Face CLI.

> [!NOTE] vLLM's OpenAI-compatible API makes it easy to integrate with existing tools and SDKs—no need to rewrite client code.

> [!IMPORTANT] Always verify which precision and quantization options your model supports and test memory usage to avoid out-of-memory failures.

## Takeaways

- vLLM provides a straightforward path to serve models locally with fast inference and many production-focused features. With a proper virtual environment, Hugging Face token when required, and attention to VRAM and quantization choices, you can run and expose powerful models via an OpenAI-compatible endpoint for local or networked applications.
